cards.text: Friend, the prophet Hosea is in the middle of a hard message for Israel. He opens with a picture: “Israel was a luxuriant vine, yielding fruit for himself.” Israel is THRIVING.

cards.question: But watch what Israel does with all that fruit. The more the fruit increased, the more Israel increased the ___.
As Israel's land produced better, Israel tore down its sacred pillars.

cards.text: Then Hosea says it plain: their hearts are devious, and now they must bear their guilt. Not confused, not having an off week. DEVIOUS.

cards.question: Israel has been building up altars and sacred pillars. So what will the LORD do to them?

cards.text: Next, Hosea tells what the people will say about having a king. And friend, it is NOT a pep rally.

cards.question: The people will say, 'We have no king.' What reason do they give?

answers.text: We do not revere the LORD

cards.question: Then the people say a king can do a lot for them.

cards.text: Their promises are mere words, and they make covenants with false oaths. It's like me telling a baker, 'I'll keep this story short,' and friend, I have NEVER kept a story short.

cards.question: All those broken promises grow into something. Judgment springs up like poisonous ___ in the furrows of a field.

cards.text: Now Hosea turns to the calf of Beth-aven. He says the people of Samaria will fear for it.

cards.question: The calf's people and its idolatrous priests will mourn over the calf of Beth-aven. Why?

answers.text: It is taken from them into exile
It is melted down in a fire
It is smashed by a prophet

cards.question: The calf of Beth-aven gets carried off to ___ as tribute to the great king.

cards.text: Hosea says Ephraim and Israel in the same breath: Ephraim will be seized with shame, and Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.

cards.question: When Samaria is carried off, Hosea says her king will be left behind.

cards.text: Samaria goes with her king, carried off “like a twig on the surface of the water.” Just floating wherever the water says.
The high places of Aven will be destroyed, and Hosea calls it the sin of Israel. Thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars.

cards.question: Then the people of Israel call out to the mountains and the hills. What do they want?

cards.text: Then Hosea reaches way back to Gibeah, where a horrible crime once ended in war (Judges 19–20). He says, “Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel.”

cards.question: Hosea says Israel has moved far past the sins of Gibeah.

cards.text: Nope: “and there you have remained.” Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in a junk drawer, and even I think that's a long time to stay put.
Then the LORD says He will chasten them when He pleases.

cards.question: ___ will be gathered against Israel to put them in bondage for their double transgression.

cards.text: New picture: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh.

cards.question: But the LORD has other plans for that heifer. He says, 'I will place a ___ on her fair neck.'
The LORD says He will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow, and Jacob will break the hard ground.

cards.text: And then comes an invitation: “Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground.” I know hard ground, friend: I once baked a batch so hard it's STILL holding a door open somewhere.

cards.question: Israel is told to break up the unplowed ground. Why now?

answers.text: It is time to seek the LORD
The ground will soon be sold

cards.question: Israel is told to sow righteousness. If they seek the LORD until He comes, what will He send on them like rain?

cards.text: But here's what they actually did: they plowed wickedness, reaped injustice and ate the fruit of lies.

cards.question: Hosea says Israel trusted in their own way. What else did Israel trust in?

answers.text: The multitude of their mighty men

cards.text: So the roar of battle will rise against Israel's people.

cards.question: Hosea says Israel's fortresses will stand strong through the battle.

cards.text: Hosea compares it to the day Shalman devastated Beth-arbel, when mothers were dashed to pieces along with their children. It's a terrible picture, and Hosea doesn't soften it.
Then Hosea names a place: “Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel, because of your great wickedness.”

cards.question: And when the day dawns, what happens to the king of Israel?

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 has a dash outside a quotation: "Then Hosea reaches way back to Gibeah, where a horrible crime once ended in war (Judges 19–20). He says, “Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel.”"

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The right answer 'We do not revere the LORD' is the only one that mentions the LORD and the only one in biblical wording. The wrong answers ('Our king grew too old', 'Our king lost a battle') are plain and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This card is a bare restatement of the verse with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It also gives no context for what the calf of Beth-aven is or where Samaria is, so the moment doesn't make sense to a baker who meets them here for the first time.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Ephraim appears for the first time and isn't identified as a name for the northern kingdom of Israel. The line 'Ephraim and Israel in the same breath' points out a pairing without telling the baker who Ephraim is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card ties Hosea's 'days of Gibeah' to the crime and war of Judges 19–20. Hosea 10:9 never says which events at Gibeah it means, so the card states a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: This story card is a single flat line ('Then the LORD says He will chasten them when He pleases.') with no Papa Dorin voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This story card is a single flat line ('New picture: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh.') with no Papa Dorin voice and no help with what the heifer picture means.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This true-or-false card restates verse 11's wording, and no earlier card gives the baker anything to reason from. Judah and Jacob are also new and aren't identified. The baker can only guess at the wording, which makes the card luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Judah and Jacob appear for the first time without being identified. Judah is the southern kingdom, and Jacob here is a name for Israel.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Verse 12's core action is breaking up unplowed ground. The joke is only about something being hard (cookies holding a door open) and has no breaking up in it, so it rides on the word 'hard' rather than the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question begins 'Israel is told to sow righteousness' and then asks what He sends like rain. The right answer is 'Righteousness', so the question's own setup points to it and rules out 'Riches' and 'Victory'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card is a single flat line ('So the roar of battle will rise against Israel's people.') with no Papa Dorin voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
